# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for answering questions)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Movie Boys in Peril; or, Strenuous Days Along the Panama Canal" by Victor Appleton (Garden City Publishing, 1926; Gutenberg 76378)

**Main characters:** Joe Duncan and Blake Stewart, "Moving Picture Boys," operators with a motor cycle bought jointly. Blake is the more serious, deeper thinker; Joe is the impulsive one with a head for figures and a patent pending on a focusing tube. Their chum-pledge: "stick together." Friends/company: Mr. Calvert Hadley (their employer, Film Theatrical Co.), Mr. Ringold (dramatic side), C. C. Piper ("Gloomy," grouchy actor), Birdie Lee (Blake's sweetheart-tease), Mabel Pierce (new member; Joe's interest), Nettie Shay (Miss Shay), Henry Robertson. Farm/Central Falls: Mr. Hiram Baker (farm landlord), Mrs. Baker, Hank Duryee (town livery driver), horse Rex (killed), Sam (red-haired barefoot son of a farmer neighbor), Sim Rolinson (postmaster). Hotel at Central Falls. Canal people: Captain Watson (tug *Nama* captain), Captain Martail (Brazilian steamer captain, distant relative of Alcando), Captain Wiltsey (tug *Bohio* captain; Canal employee), Ramo (educated Indian guide), General George W. Goethals (chief engineer, mentioned). Villain: Vigues Alcando (Spanish/South American, of Equatorial/Brazilian railroad; "Mr. Alcando"; card reads *Vigues Alcando*), also "Hank" and "the Spaniard."

**Plot in order:**
1. Ch I-II: At farm near Central Falls (vacation), Joe and Blake on motor cycle see Hank's buggy with horse Rex run away (rein broke) toward broken bridge over deep ravine (~100 ft) at a sharp curve to temporary road. They ride motor cycle, cut across field, motor dies (gasoline pipe busted); horse plunges through barrier and dies in gulch. Carriage hangs on king beam; boys pull it back.
2. Ch III-IV: Alcando (dazed, cut on head) introduced; carries a letter addressed to both boys from Film Theatrical Co. Letter from Mr. Hadley: introduces Alcando, mentions "when you go to Panama."
3. Ch V: Sam brings a delayed special-delivery letter (postmaster Sim gave it to Sam's father, who carried it in pocket). Full Hadley letter: Panama trip, big Culebra Cut slide predicted, Alcando a student. Boys decide to go.
4. Ch VI-VII: Blake's suspicion; Blake reads *History of the Panama Canal* at Central Falls library. Alcando's letter fragment "go to Panama, get all the pictures you can, especially the big guns" — Alcando explains "guns/ones" error. Visit to Alcando's hotel room (odor of cigar; a visitor slipped out). Blake sees a small box with metal projections hidden under papers.
5. Ch VIII: New York. Piper gloomy ("buried alive under one of the big Culebra slides"). Hadley briefs them: steamer to Colon, Washington Hotel headquarters, government permits; Alcando's address an uptown hotel. Departure: Birdie Lee, Mabel Pierce wave; Piper: "look out for the big slides."
6. Ch IX-X: Steamer *Gatun* to Colon via San Juan, Porto Rico. Ticking box found in Alcando's bunk (brass-bound box, metal projections); Alcando claims it's "new alarm clock" invention. Night on balcony at Colon hotel: Alcando and another man conspire ("Are you sure the machine works right?" / "Perfectly").
7. Ch XI-XII: Government tug *Nama* (Captain Watson). Runner from Spanish-speaking man: "You will not fail us?" Alcando: "I will not fail." Locks at Gatun: steel chain fender, gates; tug gets pulled backward toward closing gates (signal failure) – stopped in time.
8. Ch XIII-XIV: Gatun locks, Gatun Dam (1.5 mi long, 105 ft high). Captain warns dynamite is only threat. Jungle trip up Chagres; leaf-cutting ants, tapirs, orchids ("Holy Ghost"), iguanas (legs tied), mamaei and sapodilla fruits. Blake attacked by alligator while swimming (cramp after plantains); Joe saves him; guide Ramo shoots alligator with rifle.
9. Ch XV-XVI: Culebra Cut; Alcando mutters "Yes, dynamite here, or at the dam, would do the work"; claims he was speaking abstractly. Gold Hill. Boys stay two weeks; Hadley letter praises work.
10. Ch XVI-XVII: Brazilian steamer (Captain Martail; Alcando waves to it) crashes tug *Nama* against Pedro Miguel/Miraflores central pier; *Nama* sinks. Boys move to *Bohio* (Captain Wiltsey). Later, at Miraflores, an upper lock gate opens by mistake; emergency steel dam swung into place (electrical, 2 min; hand 30 min). Boys film it with two cameras; Alcando films too (brave).
11. Ch XVIII-XIX: Big slide in Culebra Cut (rains). Joe buried under slide with camera, wrapped in rubber coat; Blake and Alcando dig; Indian worker runs for men. Joe rescued unconscious, bleeding forehead; doctor at Gatun.
12. Ch XX-XXI: Joe recovers; Blake works at Culebra a week. Joe suspicious of Alcando's muttering ("I just hate to do it… I'll not put the blame on…"). Blake thinks Alcando failed at moving pictures.
13. Ch XXII-XXIII: Alcando's ticking box in film-case. Letter fragment: "Stuff is all ready for you. You had better do the job and get away. There is some fine scenery in Europe." Captain Wiltsey warns of dynamite plot on Gatun Dam to-night.
14. Ch XXIV-XXV: Boys set automatic flash camera + two hand cameras near spillway; hear ticking; find brass box with wires; Blake cuts wires with pliers. Alcando caught in the glare near spillway. Alcando confesses: plot by stockholder of Brazilian railroad to damage/scare Canal; small charge only; planned to blame boys; "Alcando" ran off next morning, never caught. Stockholder and Alcando later seen in Europe.
15. Ch XXVI-XXVII (end): Boys leave; Blake says he'll return to New York. Final: "The Movie Boys Under the Sea" is next volume.

**Series list (back matter):** The Movie Boys on Call; in the Wild West; and the Wreckers; in the Jungle; in Earthquake Land; and the Flood; in Peril; Under the Sea; Under Fire; Under Uncle Sam; First Showhouse; at Seaside Park; on Broadway; Outdoor Exhibition; New Idea; at the Big Fair; War Spectacle. (Also Frank Allen, Nat Ridley, Dave Fearless series ads.)

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Layton Court Mystery" by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg 72883; text ed. Doubleday, Doran 1929; first pub. 1926 anonymously)

**Dedication:** "To my Father." Preface notes author's fair-play approach and that detective makes mistakes.

**Main characters:**
- **Roger Sheringham** (narrator-ish detective; author of detective novels; under 40, over 30; short, stocky, round face, grey eyes; big-bowled pipe; Winchester & Oxford; half-blue in golf; garish grey flannel trousers, old Norfolk jacket). Talkative, dramatic, enjoys deduction; "Sherlock" nickname from Alec.
- **Alec (Alexander) Grierson**: large broad-shouldered, cheerful, Oxford cricketer (3 years for Oxford), Scottish ("Alexander Watson" joke; Watson to Roger's Holmes). Engaged to Barbara Shannon; then broken off.
- **Barbara Shannon**: small, slight, large grey eyes, fair hair, age ~19, firm chin. Daughter of Mrs. Shannon.
- **Mrs. Shannon**: small, fair, doll-like, insipid, peevish, complains of birds and dogs.
- **Victor Stanworth**: host at Layton Court, Herts; ~60, genial, red face, half-crown cigars, pre-war whisky; bachelor; City financier (directorships); Mecca = City; younger brother married Lady Cynthia Anglemere (daughter of Earl of Grassingham); settles £1,000/yr on her. Found dead, shot in centre of forehead, in the library, revolver in right hand. Typed suicide note: "To Whom it May Concern. For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself." Signed "Victor Stanworth" with earlier attempt "V-i-c".
- **Lady Stanworth** (Cynthia): tall, stately, greying hair, cool, dislikes Victor; secretly married Jefferson ~6 months earlier (Lady Jefferson). Victor had hold over her (threatened exposure of her father, the earl, or her affairs; she had chosen to marry his brother).
- **Major Harry Jefferson**: tall, thin, sallow, taciturn, ex-army (Indian regiment), Stanworth's secretary-dogsbody. Past: took blame for brother-officer's forged check; Stanworth got check and blackmailed him into job.
- **Graves** (real name Bill Higgins): butler, ex-prize-fighter, huge, Stanworth's hold over him (could have had him hanged).
- **Mrs. Mary Plant**: graceful dark-haired, ~26, husband in Soudanese Civil Service; jewels; blackmailed by Stanworth over pre-marriage incident; faints when told of death. Preferred scent *Parfum Jasmine* (9s 6d); *Amour des Fleurs* a guinea.
- **Doctor Matthewson**: examined Stanworth for hay fever.
- **Inspector Mansfield** of Elchester police: methodical; constable Rudgeman.
- **William**: gardener, melancholy, hates greenfly; wife (Mrs. William) at lodge; Chapman the chauffeur (car, Sunbeam). Cook's "brother" (a large man, seen 8:30 pm). Maids: Alice, Mary.
- **Mr. Wetherby**: farmer at Hillcrest Farm; **John Prince** (suspected murderer per Mrs. William, actually a red herring; "Prince John").
- Landlord and ancient rustic at village inn (bull chase).

**Plot in order:**
1. Ch I: 8 a.m., Layton Court rose garden; William troubled by greenfly. Roger meets Alec, who has posted a letter at village (claims to bookmaker). Alec had just been jilted by Barbara that morning ("I can't marry you").
2. Ch II: Background on Stanworth; guests: Alec, Roger, Barbara, Mrs. Shannon, Mrs. Plant, Major Jefferson, Lady Stanworth, Graves. Breakfast; Jefferson leaves when Graves reports something. Lady Stanworth summons Roger and Alec; library door locked; Jefferson, Graves, Alec and Roger break it open. Stanworth found dead.
3. Ch III: Library described (Jacobean, French windows, sash window, lattice window, safe, typewriter table, black settee). Typed confession; Roger notes odd signature; Jefferson sends Roger to tell women; Mrs. Plant faints; Mrs. Plant found at safe claiming she wanted her jewels. Jefferson tries to get Roger out of library.
4. Ch IV: Inspector Mansfield; Dr. Matthewson: died ~2 a.m., one shot, bullet extracted; safe keys in Stanworth's upper waistcoat pocket; Jefferson reluctant to open safe; ashes in grate noted by Roger.
5. Ch V: Interviews: Jefferson last saw Stanworth ~10 p.m. (Roger present); Roger last with Stanworth in garden, then to hall with Mrs. Plant. Alec engaged to Barbara day before.
6. Ch VI: Roger points out shot placement (forehead, unnatural); suspects inconsistencies (Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, Lady Stanworth, butler; missing second vase; keys in wrong pocket; scratch on wrist).
7. Ch VII: Vase clue: two blue vases, one gone; ring in dust; pieces of blue china on hearth; Roger says vase shot — bullet hole behind pillar on left of chimney-piece. Alec and Barbara talk in garden (she refuses to explain).
8. Ch VIII: Roger's murder theory. Second shot from Stanworth's gun? Only one shell in revolver. Roger: murdered; inspector arriving; Alec: suicide. Confession possibly faked (signature)—Roger's theory.
9. Ch IX: Lunch. Roger sees Jefferson's behaviour as relieved; visions. Footprints/scrap of paper in waste-paper basket: Roger finds the typed confession was made on a sheet with Stanworth's signature and fountain-pen testing marks; theory: confession is fake.
10. Ch X: Roger's murder theory (Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, lies). Mrs. Plant's jewels; Roger queries her; Alec defends her.
11. Ch XI: Safe opened; cash-box ~£4,000; Mrs. Plant's jewels; Lady Stanworth's odd reaction; Jefferson's "nothing of importance."
12. Ch XII-XIII: Secret door search; lattice window with handle trick; footprint (large, ~10-11 boot) under window; Roger demonstrates handle lock; Jefferson overhears.
13. Ch XIV: Ash pit: scrap of pencil letter: "...frightened ... this neighbourhood ... serious danger ... that brute Prince ..." Investigation of John Prince; Mrs. William says Prince attacked Stanworth earlier and is dangerous.
14. Ch XV-XVI: Village inn; landlord says Prince at agricultural show at Elchester yesterday; Prince at Hillcrest Farm (Wetherby); bull chase. Stations inquiries; William says large man seen ~8:30 pm, cook's brother.
15. Ch XVII-XVIII: Footprints found smoothed (someone heard them). Roger drops theories. Mrs. Plant tells slightly different story; Roger finds blue vase pieces in laurel shrubbery between library and dining room.
16. Ch XIX-XXI: Roger finds 'cash payments' in passbooks: Stanworth was a blackmailer. Roger hypothesises Jefferson killed Stanworth for Mrs. Plant.
17. Ch XXII-XXIII: Inquest: suicide during temporary insanity. Mrs. Plant admits she was blackmailed; she says Jefferson never came into library; she received typed suicide letter posted in village by 8:30 post (so Stanworth could not have posted it).
18. Ch XXIV-XXV: Jefferson refuses where-he-was; then reveals he was with his wife (Lady Stanworth) — they're married secretly; Roger's Jefferson-murder theory collapses.
19. Ch XXVI-XXVII: Roger questions Jefferson about Stanworth's hold: his forgery story; Roger realises Mrs. Plant's note was posted after death. Roger concludes second woman in library: hair (Barbara's colour). Alec admits privately.
20. Ch XXVIII (confession): **Alec killed Stanworth.** Night of murder: Alec went to library at night in pyjamas for a book; hid behind curtain; heard Mrs. Plant weeping over blackmail; Barbara then came in — Stanworth was blackmailing her mother Mrs. Shannon (he demanded Barbara marry Alec and pay money). Barbara defied him and left. Alec came out; Stanworth fired and missed (hit vase); Alec twisted gun to his forehead and fired. Alec removed one shell, burnt blackmail papers in safe, typed letters to Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, Lady Stanworth (and typed fake confession), locked lattice window via handle trick, went back in through dining room. Alec asks whether to tell police; Roger says no (though not formally resolved). Last line: Roger: "try sometimes not to be so disgustingly conventional!"

**Key clues/facts to keep:** Shot from 2 a.m. approx; Stanworth shot at centre of forehead; footprint size ~10-11; typed confession with fountain-pen marks; second vase shot; ashes in grate; hair on settee (Barbara's); scent *Parfum Jasmine* handkerchief (Mrs. Plant's—Roger's bet); powder on settee arm; keys in upper waistcoat pocket; Jefferson-Lady Stanworth secret marriage; Mrs. Plant's letter posted 8:30 village post; Graves/Higgins; Prince red herring; cook's brother seen 8:30 p.m.
